# Target tiers

<!-- generated by scripts/wj/target_tiers.wj from tests/conformance/backend_results.tsv and backend_ledger.tsv; do not edit -->

What each backend can run today, measured by the conformance programs (`tests/conformance`) and the spec's run cases (`tests/spec`) ([ADR-0007](adr/0007-target-tiers-conformance.md)).
**Tier 1**: every program passes, no exception. **Tier 2**: experimental; the programs that fail are listed below, exactly, with the reason. `not run`: the toolchain is not installed on the machine that measured; the commands to fill it in are at the end.

| Backend | Tier | conformance | spec run cases | failing | not run |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| rust | Tier 2 | 24/28 | 222/231 | 13 | 0 |
| javascript | Tier 2 | 17/28 | 204/231 | 38 | 0 |
| typescript | Tier 2 | 17/28 | 204/231 | 38 | 0 |
| go | Tier 2 | 16/28 | 197/231 | 46 | 0 |
| wasm | Tier 2 | 17/28 | 194/231 | 48 | 0 |
| interpreter | Tier 2 | 23/28 | 231/231 | 5 | 0 |

## Failing programs (the ledger)

The ledger is `tests/conformance/backend_ledger.tsv`: it only shrinks (`target_tiers.wj check` fails when a listed program passes, or when a failing program is not listed).

### wasm

- `conformance/concurrency/channels` (build): the wasm build of the same generated Rust fails like the rust backend's (E0433: crate `windjammer_runtime` is not linked by the plain-rustc harness); it also uses `std::thread::spawn`/`Condvar` in `windjammer_runtime::task`, unavailable on wasm32-wasip1 | plan: ADR-0004 stage 3 for wasm (docs/concurrency/WASM_EXECUTOR_PLAN.md): even with the runtime crate linked, windjammer_runtime::task spawns std::thread, which wasm32-wasip1 does not provide, so the cooperative single-thread executor is needed: a BETA item | measured with the plain-rustc harness before it built through cargo: the rust row of this program now passes, so re-measure on the PC (`target_tiers.wj run <wj> --backend wasm --only <program>`); if it still fails, the cause is the thread-based `windjammer_runtime::task` (WASM_EXECUTOR_PLAN.md)

## Notes on wasm

- `wasm` is the Rust backend's output built for `wasm32-wasip1` and run under `wasmtime` (the WebAssembly platform); a machine without `wasmtime` and `rustup target add wasm32-wasip1` records `not-run` and keeps the rows another machine measured. The rows above were measured on the PC. `wj build -t wasm` itself emits a browser library (a wasm-bindgen cdylib crate) with no headless runner, so that target is not covered by this row.
- Why wasm programs fail: every wasm failure is also a failure of the same program on the rust backend (the same generated Rust does not compile or is wrong: listed under rust), or a panic-mode program that passes on rust but whose wasm build aborts instead of unwinding, so the exit status is not 101 (the 13 panic cases below; expected cause, to be confirmed with `wasmtime run`).

## Filling in what this machine could not run

A machine with the toolchains runs `wj run scripts/wj/target_tiers.wj run <wj-binary> --backend <name>` (names: rust, javascript, typescript, go, wasm, interpreter; needs rustc, node >= 22.6, go, wasmtime plus the wasm32-wasip1 target respectively), commits `tests/conformance/backend_results.tsv` and `docs/TARGET_TIERS.md`, and adds a ledger line with a reason for every failure.
